business_problem: First Abu Dhabi Bank needed a faster way for relationship managers and advisers to spot and validate sustainable finance opportunities because manually scanning news, market updates, and sustainability data was slow and hard to scale against its ambitious capital deployment target.
solution_summary: First Abu Dhabi Bank worked with Bain and the World Economic Forum to build Sustainable Finance Market Pulse, an AI-powered lead identification tool for sustainable finance. After an eight-week sprint to size the value of AI across 18 candidate use cases, the team shortlisted five options and built a prototype around the highest-value one. Pulse operates as an AI agent that mirrors the manual workflow of human advisers: it reviews more than 1,500 market signals across eight countries, validates opportunities, prioritizes them, and returns a vetted pipeline to users. The tool is also positioned as the first module in a broader sustainability intelligence platform that can support tracking, reporting, and transaction efficiency. The story does not identify a separate storage platform, but it clearly describes upstream market and sustainability data feeding a decision-support layer that relationship teams can use immediately in pilot.

data_flow: News, market updates, and sustainability data feed Sustainable Finance Market Pulse, where the AI agent reviews signals across countries, validates opportunities, and prioritizes them into a vetted list. Relationship managers and advisers then use that ranked output to pursue sustainable finance deals more quickly.
business_outcome: During pilot, Market Pulse surfaced dozens of vetted opportunities and gave FAB a scalable way to prioritize sustainable finance leads, with modeled revenue and capital-deployment upside that could materially expand the bank's sustainability program.
